newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel steady, U.S. demand holds up.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel steady, U.S. demand holds up.

text.p: Straight-run fuel oil markets were steady on Tuesday, with trans-Atlantic demand underpinning recovery from recent lows, traders said.
An Irish refinery was heard to have sold 27,000 tonnes of low sulphur, loading end-month, into Britain for $94.75 fob.
The price, while not low, widened the bid/offer spread as better quality British and Scandinavia was heard offered at $98 fob with interest from trans-Atlantic buyers into May.
Some 200,000 tonnes of material is believed to have headed west in the last two weeks.
Daewoo in Antwerp continues to supply material into the inland European barge market, with 10,000 tonnes sold on Monday at $95.50 fob and 9,000 tonnes sold today on a floating price basis.
Russian straight-run E-4s were heard moving out of the Baltics at a rate of around two to three a week, with premiums of $2-$3 for good quality material, with BP still the main buyer.
A cargo of M100 aboard the Alba from Tallin was heard traded at two means plus $6.50.
